name: Plate Pinch
summary: An isometric grip exercise where one or more weight plates are held between the thumb and fingers to build pinching strength and forearm endurance.

setup: Position one thick plate or two smooth-faced plates together standing upright on the floor or a low bench.
Stand tall alongside the weight with feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and grasp the rim or face of the plate(s) using only the pads of your fingers on one side and your thumb on the opposite side.
steps: Squeeze the plate(s) forcefully between your fingers and thumb.
Deadlift the weight smoothly off the floor by extending your hips and knees until standing fully upright.
Hold the plate stationary at your side with your arm extended and shoulders packed for the target duration.
Hinge at the hips to return the plate under control to the floor before grip failure occurs, then switch sides.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and evenly throughout the hold while maintaining abdominal bracing.
cues: Stand tall without leaning to the side

common_faults.fault: Resting the plate against the leg for support.
common_faults.correction: Hold the arm slightly away from the body so the weight hangs purely by grip strength.

common_faults.fault: Curling the fingers under the rim of the plate.
common_faults.correction: Keep the fingers and thumb extended flat against the smooth sides to ensure a pure pinch grip.

common_faults.fault: Holding until complete failure and dropping the plate on feet.
common_faults.correction: Terminate the set a few seconds before total failure and lower the plate safely with control.

precautions: Ensure your feet are positioned clear of the drop zone beneath the plate.
Keep the spine neutral when picking up and lowering the plates.
